name: Chakhchoukha
subtitle: Chakhchoukha is an Algerian dish of crumbled semolina dough or torn bread soaked in a red tomato sauce with lamb, chickpeas, onions and spices.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Pieces of torn bread in tomato sauce, with lamb, chickpeas, onions and several spices added.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: In eastern Algeria, a dish of crumbled semolina dough moistened with a red sauce and served with meat.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: The dish comes from Biskra, the gateway to the Algerian Sahara.

facts.label: Where it is eaten
facts.value: Very popular in Biskra and in several other regions of Algeria, each of which has its own version.

facts.label: History
facts.value: According to some, the first to make it were shepherds of the Algerian steppes who needed a hot, spicy dish for freezing winter nights.

facts.label: When it is eaten
facts.value: On Mouloud (the Prophet's birthday), eastern Algeria serves chakhchoukha, while Algiers serves rechta.

facts.label: Date
facts.value: In April 2024 the food guide TasteAtlas ranked it 17th in a list of the world's stews.

parts.text: Chakhchoukha is an Algerian dish of crumbled semolina dough or torn bread soaked in a red tomato sauce with lamb, chickpeas, onions and spices. It comes from Biskra, at the edge of the Algerian Sahara, and is popular there and in several other regions, each with its own version. One account says it was first made by shepherds of the Algerian steppes who needed a hot, spicy dish for cold winter nights.
In eastern Algeria it is the dish served on Mouloud, the Prophet's birthday.
